name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
role: Austrian-American actor and bodybuilder; Republican governor of California (2003-2011)
summary: Schwarzenegger governed California as a self-described fiscally conservative, socially liberal centrist, pledging post-partisanship. He signed the nation's first greenhouse-gas cap (AB 32), proposed universal health insurance, backed some gun limits, and supported abortion rights and domestic partnerships while twice vetoing same-sex marriage bills. Since leaving office he has campaigned on climate and against gerrymandering, condemned the January 6 attack, and endorsed Kamala Harris in 2024 while stating disagreements with her platform.

universal-healthcare.rationale: As governor he proposed a system of universal health insurance for Californians in January 2007, built on a coverage requirement with shared costs rather than a state-run system; he vetoed single-payer bills in 2006 and 2008 and derided a single-payer alternative.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said in 2004 that Republicans have 'faith in free enterprise' and that families spend money better than government does; in his 2024 statement he criticized Republican economic policy as opposed to free markets.

state-harmful.rationale: Used the state actively as governor (infrastructure bonds, climate law, health insurance proposal) and calls for 'public servants' with a 'servant's heart', treating public service as a positive.

limit-guns.rationale: In 2003 favored an assault-weapons ban and background checks; as governor signed the .50 BMG rifle ban (2004) and the pistol microstamping law (2007). No statement found calling for strict limits on ownership generally.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Vetoed legalization bills in 2005 and 2007 (saying he backed domestic partnerships), but in 2004 said same-sex marriage via the family code would be 'fine', accepted the 2008 state Supreme Court ruling, opposed the Proposition 8 ban and did not appeal the ruling striking it down. A later explicit 'should be legal' statement was not found, so medium.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as pro-choice, while supporting parental notification for minors and a ban on late-stage ('partial-birth') procedures.

free-trade.rationale: As governor led trade missions to Japan, China and Mexico, saying 'the world is California's marketplace', and promoted contracts with Chinese firms.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In 2004 said America 'fights not for imperialism but for human rights and democracy' and backed the Iraq war; later (2006) urged a deadline for withdrawal. Position on intervention for human rights is implied rather than stated in general terms.

limit-growth.rationale: In 2023 said 'we need a new environmentalism based on building and growing'; old environmentalism 'was afraid of growth'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Signed AB 32 (2006) capping California greenhouse gases and set an 80% cut by 2050 goal; said 'we simply must do everything in our power to slow down global warming'; in 2023 called climate an emergency.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 2023 said fossil fuels can only be replaced 'with renewable energy. Or nuclear energy, one or the other'. No explicit call to expand nuclear power found.

central-planning.rationale: Describes seeing communism and socialist Austria as reasons he became a Republican; endorses free enterprise and getting government 'off your back'.

one-party-rule.rationale: Condemns communist one-party rule from his own experience and pledged 'post-partisanship', calling for working with the other side.

democracy-best.rationale: Jan 6 2021 video: democracy 'held firm', is like tempered steel, and must be put first; says rejecting an election result is 'un-American'.

direct-votes.rationale: Repeatedly used ballot initiatives to bypass the legislature (2005 special election Props 74-77, Prop 11 redistricting) and endorsed Props 62/71. In 2025 he urged voters to reject a legislature-backed redistricting map and defended the independent commission voters created.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said in 2004 that 'it doesn't make any difference where you were born' and 'no matter the nationality, no matter the religion, no matter the ethnic background, America brings out the best in people.'

results-over-ideology.rationale: Governed as a self-described centrist and pledged post-partisanship; in 2024 said policy 'requires working with the other side' and that he likes to help 'make people's lives better with policies'.

individual-rights-only.rationale: 2004: a Republican believes 'a person should be treated as an individual, not as a member of an interest group'.

total-state.rationale: Said government should be 'accountable to the people, not the people to the government', a limited-government framing at odds with state direction of all areas of life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said in 2004 that the US 'fights not for imperialism but for human rights and democracy'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Signed the Civil Rights Act of 2005 and a ban on gender discrimination in health insurance; issued 2004 order barring sex-based discrimination in state personnel decisions.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Signed civil-rights and nondiscrimination laws and a 2004 order barring race-based decisions in state employment.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposed offshore drilling (2003, and joined governors in 2008 to block it); in 2023 and 2025 urged replacing fossil fuels and ending dependence on them.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: In 2006 criticized Mexican immigrants for trying to 'stay Mexican' rather than assimilate; reported remark, no fuller statement found.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said in 2024 'I hate politics and don't trust most politicians'; in 2025 called lawmakers who avoid immigration reform 'political hacks, party hacks, rather than public servants'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: As governor backed a broad state role: $42-43 billion infrastructure bonds, a universal insurance plan, the climate law and school nutrition rules.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says it makes no difference where people were born or who their parents were; signed laws barring discrimination by race, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says America brings out the best in people of every ethnic background and 'we are one America'. (He also complained in 2006 that Mexican immigrants 'try to stay Mexican'.)

death-penalty.rationale: Allowed the executions of Donald Beardslee (2005) and Stanley Williams (2005), denying clemency, and a third in 2006.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Signed the Civil Rights Act of 2005 (extending the Unruh Act on public accommodations) and the 2006 Civil Rights Housing Act.

defeat-communism.rationale: Credits the US with ending the Soviet threat he saw as a child ('the world no longer fears the Soviet Union and it is because of the United States') and calls terrorism more insidious than communism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Signed numerous LGBT-protection laws (hate crimes, nondiscrimination, domestic partner rights) and is described as signing more pro-LGBT laws than any prior California governor.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Signed gender-identity nondiscrimination provisions (2004, 2006 state programs) but vetoed a 2006 school bill covering gender identity; no direct statement on legal recognition.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Pledged an era of 'post-partisanship' (2007) and has argued that parties must move away from extremes; in 2024 said he is an American before a Republican.

recognise-genocide.rationale: In 2005 declared April 24 a Day of Remembrance of the Armenian genocide.

dense-cities.rationale: Signed a 2008 bill to coordinate local planning to curb suburban sprawl as part of climate policy; no direct statement on density.

future-generations.rationale: At AB 32 signing: reducing warming is 'something we owe our children and our grandchildren'.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Proposed a balanced-budget constitutional amendment (2008) and a constitutional spending limit with 2004 bonds.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Joined three former governors in 2004 to oppose Proposition 66, which would have weakened California's three-strikes law.

notes: Views shifted over time: same-sex marriage (vetoed legalization 2005 and 2007; by 2008 opposed the Proposition 8 ban and in 2010 did not appeal its overturning), climate (from AB 32 to 'new environmentalism' stressing fast permitting), and party stance (RNC speaker for Bush in 2004; criticized Trump and endorsed Harris in 2024). Many statements are null because no direct position was found; the 2004 speech and 2003 call-in are older than the recent record. The 2005 minimum-wage veto and his 2005-2010 tax and union positions are mixed, so left null. A later explicit statement on same-sex marriage or guns was searched for but not found.
